promptHead: Athlete goal: 5K (Corrowmore Harvest 5K) on Sun Nov 15 2026, 10 weeks out, target run the whole way.

new.headline: Keep the same three run days and grow each one by a minute or two, with full rest days between. That is the fastest safe route to running the whole 5K on Sun Nov 15.

answers.question: I want to be ready for the 5K in November. Should I run every day next week to get there faster?
answers.answer: No, please do not run every day next week. You would get there slower, not faster, because new runners' bones, tendons and calves need the off days to adapt, and that is where injuries creep in. Three run days with rest between them is exactly the right dose for someone 10 weeks in, and we have time to build you to the full 5K from here. The faster path is small, steady weekly growth plus the dog walks you already do.

new.analysis:
The big win this week was starting and completing all three sessions at an easy effort with zero pain. That is the foundation we build on, and nothing matters more right now than keeping that streak going for another week.

The plan grows total run time from about 64 to about 70 minutes, roughly a 10 percent step, which is the ceiling for a safe weekly increase. Saturday becomes your slightly longer session so your body learns to stay on its feet a little longer, and Monday and Wednesday stay familiar.

Keep your walk-run ratio as it is this week; we will lengthen the running interval in a couple of weeks once this volume feels routine. Effort stays easy, meaning you could talk in short sentences during the running portions. If your calves still feel tight at the start of a run, add two extra minutes of walking before you start the first run interval.

With 10 weeks to Nov 15, the shape of the plan is: four more weeks of gradual growth, then a few weeks of longer run intervals, then a short taper. You are on track.
